title: Rerootable Hypertree Decompositions
summary: Hypertree decompositions are a cornerstone in the theory of answering conjunctive queries efficiently. However, they are not yet widely adopted in practice. Problems related to, e.g., the uniqueness of decompositions and succinct representations of all decompositions have so far mostly been neglected by the theory literature. In this paper, we present the first in-depth discussion of rerootability in hypertree decompositions---a property which we argue is essential for such problems. Rerootability leads us to projection-freeness, and we have to discuss normal form to recover tractability. Normal form, however, again obstructs rerootability, and for this reason, we define a relaxed notion of normal form which leads to a truly rerootable and tractable class. Experimental evidence suggests that the price we pay in terms of width increase for transitioning to this class of decompositions is moderate in practice.

title: Flow-Join++: Skew-aware Distributed Joins with Cardinality-based Heavy Hitter Prediction
summary: In distributed data processing for OLAP workloads, data skew is a critical issue when joins are involved. This skew causes a load imbalance as heavy hitters create straggler nodes and increase execution times. One method that addresses this issue is Flow-Join, which prevents heavy hitters from being transferred and processed on a single node. However, it has two limitations: time-consuming heavy hitter detection and a lack of plan-level coordination in multi-table join workloads. In this paper, we propose Flow-Join++, a skew-aware distributed join approach that leverages a cardinality estimation model to predict heavy hitters and optimize query execution at the plan level. Flow-Join++ estimates the fanout of join keys in a single inference step, eliminating sampling overhead for heavy hitter detection. It provides a Heavy Hitter Push-Down strategy that partitions heavy hitter tuples immediately after scanning base relations, enabling coordinated skew-aware processing across multiple joins. We conducted experiments using the TPC-H benchmark with controllable skew injections, as well as the Phone Bill benchmark, which simulates realistic OLAP workloads in telecommunications services. The results validate the effectiveness of the proposed approach compared to standard join strategies.

title: Query-driven explainable join discovery of analytic cubes based on profiling
summary: The rapid growth of data repositories limits user’s awareness of their content and the understanding of interrelationships between diverse datasets, increasing the demand for effective data discovery tools that help analysts locate relevant data. Join discovery, the process of finding tables that can be joined based on common attributes, is one possible strategy. This paper introduces a novel join discovery approach tailored to data structures commonly used in analytics: multidimensional or analytic cubes. By leveraging the unique structure of analytic cubes, the approach utilizes the concept of profile , which refers to metadata providing information about data distribution. Specifically, we introduce a profile-based, query-driven join discovery model that allows users to identify alternative joinable cubes starting from a declarative query, as well as to rank and qualitatively assess alternatives. We validate the efficiency and effectiveness of our approach through extensive experimentation. Our dual approach, which combines schema-level and content-level information, enhances both the expressivity of join discovery and the clarity of join discovery results, making the analysis process more intuitive and interpretable.

title: Hyperfiniteness, Limit Laws, and Constant-Query Approximation Schemes on Canonical GIRGs
summary: Geometric inhomogeneous random graphs (GIRGs) combine sparse average degree, latent Euclidean geometry, non-vanishing clustering, and heavy-tailed degrees. Their unbounded maximum degree places them outside the bounded-degree classes for which constant-query optimization is classically understood. We prove that, in the canonical exact-kernel GIRG with fixed d≥ 1, τ> 2, and integrable geometry exponent α> 1 (including α=∞), this obstruction can be removed after an arbitrarily small linear edge-edit budget. For every η> 0, with high probability one can delete at most ηn edges and obtain a spanning graph whose connected components have size at most a constant K (η) independent of n; moreover the component of a queried vertex is discoverable with Oη (1) calls in a latent-mark RealRAM adjacency-list oracle. The proof combines a repaired quenched first-moment argument for high-degree mass, residual weight truncation, long-edge suppression, a geometry-aligned grid cut, and explicit treatment of rare oversized cells/components. This local hyperfiniteness yields a general estimator for every linearly bounded, componentadditive objective that is Lipschitz under one edge edit. For Minimum Dominating Set (MDS), the canonical GIRG has positive isolation density, so γ (Gn)= Ω (n) whp; hence the additive estimator becomes a marked constant-query (1+ ε) PTAS. A local computation algorithm answers membership queries consistently with one global dominating set D satisfying| D|≤(1+ ε) γ (Gn) whp Explicit output still requires Ω (n) time. We give a full two-root, phase-augmented proof that every stable additive objective has a deterministic density F (Gn)/n→ ρF in probability, rather than assuming that an absolute-coordinate grid is automatically covered by ordinary local convergence. Several further consequences connect local algorithms, probability, and statistical physics. The infinite marked-Poisson GIRG admits a stationary randomized bounded-component edge decomposition with arbitrarily small expected removed degree. The domination density is non-degenerate, 0< ρDS< 1, and equals the infimum asymptotic density achievable by finite-radius mark-aware local dominating-set rules (zero locality gap). The hard-constraint domination partition function has a deterministic quenched pressure for every inverse temperature β≥ 0; at β= 0 this gives a non-trivial configurational-entropy density, while for β> 0 the free-energy density converges to ρDS at zero temperature with error at most (log 2)/β. Coupling two kernels gives explicit continuity and monotonicity bounds in the geometry/softness and scale parameters, including an O (1/(α− 1)) soft-to-threshold bound. Finally, Efron–Stein yields self-averaging variance bounds O (n4− τ) for 2< τ< 3, O (n log n) at τ= 3, and O (n) for τ> 3. In the supercritical Poissonized product-GIRG regime 2< τ< 3 covered by existing giant-locality theorems, the giant component itself has domination number Ω (n), showing that linear domination is not merely an isolated-vertex artifact there.

title: CRYPTOGRAPHIC MULTI-PARTY PROTOCOLS FOR PRIVACY-PRESERVING CONFIDENTIAL DATABASE QUERIES
summary: The rapid growth of distributed computing environments, cloud databases, and collaborative data analytics has increased the need for secure mechanisms that enable organizations to perform database queries without revealing sensitive information. Traditional database query processing techniques require direct access to stored data, creating privacy risks when multiple parties share or analyze confidential datasets. Privacypreserving computation has emerged as an important approach for enabling secure collaboration while maintaining data confidentiality. This paper proposes a Cryptographic Multi-Party Protocol Framework for Privacy-Preserving Confidential Database Queries that integrates secure multi-party computation, advanced cryptographic protocols, encrypted query processing, access control mechanisms, and distributed privacy-preserving analytics. The proposed framework enables multiple data owners to collaboratively execute complex database queries while ensuring that individual datasets remain confidential throughout the computation process. Cryptographic protocols allow secure processing of encrypted information without exposing raw data to unauthorized entities. The framework supports confidential query execution, secure data sharing, privacy protection, and trustworthy collaborative analytics across distributed environments. Experimental analysis demonstrates that the proposed approach improves query confidentiality, data protection, security resilience, and collaborative computation efficiency compared with traditional database query mechanisms. The proposed solution provides a scalable and secure foundation for privacy-preserving database systems in cloud computing, healthcare, finance, and enterprise data-sharing environments. Keywords: Cryptographic Protocols, Secure Multi-Party Computation, Privacy-Preserving Queries, Confidential Databases, Data Security, Encrypted Computation, Cloud Databases, Access Control, Secure Data Sharing, Information Privacy.

title: SURT-DETR: Sea-Sky Line Context-Aware and Uncertainty-Guided Small Object Detection for Unmanned Surface Vehicles
summary: Detecting small objects within complex maritime environments presents a persistent challenge for Unmanned Surface Vehicle (USV) perception. Extreme scale variations often render distant targets as indistinct visual features, while background interference from waves and sea-sky boundaries further obscures object delineation. Consequently, state-of-the-art detectors frequently suffer from inaccurate localization and limited generalization capabilities. To address these limitations, we propose SURT-DETR, a robust Transformer-based framework tailored for USV perception. Constructed upon the RT-DETR architecture, SURT-DETR integrates three innovations: (1) the Sea-Sky Line Context-Aware Feature Enhancement Module (SLCAM) to model geometric priors and suppress background noise; (2) the Uncertainty-Guided Small Object Decoder Branch (UGSD) to enhance tiny target detection; and (3) an Uncertainty-Regularized NWD Loss to mitigate scale sensitivity and localization uncertainty. Experimental results on the Pohang Canal Dataset verify the effectiveness of our method. The SURT-DETR achieves an overall mAP of 79.5% and smallobject mAPs of 69.2%. Compared with the RT-DETR baseline, our model obtains clear accuracy gains on overall and small-target detection metrics with a modest parameter increment of 1.2M. Ablation experiments further confirm the complementarity and efficacy of the proposed modules, making the method applicable for practical USV maritime perception tasks.

title: Cost-Efficient and Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning for Cloud-Based Systems: A Comparative Analysis
summary:
As cloud-based machine learning becomes more widespread, issues of cost and data privacy have taken centre stage. This chapter explores federated learning (FL) as a decentralized alternative to traditional centralized training, with a specific focus on its costefficiency in cloud environments. The implementation was carried out on a local machine using Anaconda, where multiple clients simulated collaborative model training by sending only model updates—rather than raw data—to a central server.
To evaluate cloud impact, a cost model was built comparing centralized and federated setups. Results show that centralized training required transferring over 1.4 GB of raw data, incurring a total cloud cost of around $0.1806. In contrast, the federated approach sent just 5.625 KB of updates across 10 training rounds, bringing the total cost down to $0.0023—an impressive 98.73% reduction. While training in the federated setup took longer (216.05 seconds vs. 0.0702 seconds), compute costs remained minimal.

title: A Pan-African AI-Enabled Digital Innovation Ecosystem for Health, Education and Decent Work: Leveraging Hybrid Connectivity, Data and Frontier Technologies to …
summary: Africa's digital transformation is constrained by fragmented sector-specific platforms, uneven connectivity, and governance regimes ill-matched to a predominantly rural, cross-border population. This paper proposes a Pan-African Digital Innovation Ecosystem (PADIE): a deployable systems-engineering reference architecture integrating health, education, and decent-work services on a shared, country-anchored digital public infrastructure. The contribution is fivefold. First, a five-layer architecture coupling hybrid terrestrial / non-terrestrial networks, Open-RAN, Kubernetes-based edge AI orchestration, a federated data fabric, and a zero-trust identity and consent layer. Second, explicit cross-layer orchestration, edge-cloud workload placement, offline-first conflict-free synchronization, TN/NTN failover, identity propagation, and federated AI lifecycle management - that closes the operational gap of prior frameworks. Third, instantiation through a flagship rural telehealth-triage use case with end-to-end data flow, latency budgets, and KPIs. Fourth, an indicative Phase-1 cost model and deployment-constraint analysis for two anchor countries. Fifth, comparative positioning against the AU Digital Transformation Strategy, Smart Africa, World Bank DPI, smart city blueprints, and isolated e-health and e-learning stacks. A three-phase roadmap and a multi-level governance interaction map complete the proposal.

title: MetaSpongeDetect: A Meta-Learning Approach to Securing AI Systems Against Sponge Attacks in Social Applications
summary: As artificial intelligence (AI) technologies become increasingly integrated into critical social systems ranging from healthcare diagnostics to smart city infrastructure, their security and computational efficiency are paramount. Among emerging threats, sponge poisoning attacks exploit deep learning models to silently increase training energy and latency without impacting accuracy, posing serious availability risks in real-world deployments. This article introduces MetaSpongeDetect, a meta-learning-based detection framework designed for online identification of such stealthy adversarial behaviors. The approach leverages a recurrent neural network (RNN) within a model-agnostic meta-learning (MAML) paradigm to capture temporal patterns in the training of model dynamics. By learning from a distribution of tasks constructed from model statistics across multiple architectures and datasets, MetaSpongeDetect generalizes effectively to previously unseen attack scenarios. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior performance in few-shot settings, significantly outperforming baseline anomaly detection techniques. The framework offers a robust and scalable solution for online detection of training-time adversarial behaviors. The proposed approach enhances AI system resilience and safety, making it suitable for deployment in computational social systems, where robustness, energy efficiency, and public trust are critical. MetaSpongeDetect achieves 95%–99% detection accuracy across diverse models and datasets, demonstrating robust generalization to unseen sponge poisoning attacks. This scalable, adaptive framework enables online detection of training-time adversarial behaviors, enhancing the resilience and reliability of AI systems in computational social infrastructures.

title: TC-SpMM: A Tile-based Compression Framework for FPGA-based SpMM
summary: Sparse matrix dense matrix multiplication (SpMM) is a core kernel in scientific computing, graph analytics, and machine learning, yet remains memory bound due to irregular sparsity and limited data reuse. Classical formats such as CSR and SBR-ELL, as well as index-aligned tiling techniques, improve traversal efficiency but fundamentally treat each nonzero block independently, leading to redundant computation when similar sparse patterns recur. FPGA based SpMM accelerators have increasingly adopted block-compressed sparse row (BCSR) formats to exploit on-chip Block RAM (BRAM) for high-bandwidth, low-latency tile storage; however, these designs load and process each nonzero tile as an independent compute unit, without exploiting algebraic redundancy across structurally equivalent tiles. Duplicate tile patterns cause the same BRAM banks to be read multiple times and the same multiply-accumulate sequences to be reissued redundantly, consuming precious bandwidth, DSP cycles, and energy that could otherwise be eliminated. We propose tile-based compression with redundancy-aware scheduling (TC-SpMM), a method that identifies and categorizes duplicate sparse tiles and leverages this information to reduce storage as well as redundant computation and memory traffic during SpMM. By storing each unique tile once in BRAM and replacing all duplicate occurrences with inexpensive pointer metadata, TC-SpMM enables a single canonical tile evaluation to serve multiple logical output positions without additional synchronization or decompression overhead directly reducing BRAM read traffic and DSP utilization on FPGA platforms. Experimental evaluation across a suite of 15 sparse matrices shows more than 50% additional compression relative to CSR and BCSR for most of the matrices. Using an analytical cost model, we also obtain notable reductions in required FLOPs and memory accesses compared to baseline BCSR-based SpMM for some baseline Models, highlighting the effectiveness of combining compression with execution-aware scheduling on FPGA accelerators for sustainable computing.

title: AI based Copper Mining Profit Prediction
summary: Open-pit copper mining demands substantial upfront capital and sustained operational expenditure, making block-level profitability forecasting indispensable for reliable mine planning and sequencing. Existing estimation approaches depend heavily on fixed economic assumptions and manual formula-based calculations that fail to represent the nonlinear interdependencies among ore grade, extraction cost, and market revenue. This paper proposes a machine learning-driven profit estimation system built upon structured 3D mine block model data. Input attributes encompass spatial block coordinates, copper grade percentage, block geometry, rock density, and both mining and processing cost parameters. A comparative regression study is conducted encompassing Linear Regression, Random Forest Regressor, and XGBoost Regressor, with predictive quality measured through R2 coefficient, Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE). Findings confirm that gradient-boosted ensemble architectures substantially exceed baseline linear models in prediction fidelity and generalisation robustness. Beyond static forecasting, the system accommodates live updates to block model inputs, allowing mine planners to reassess block economics as copper prices or geological interpretations shift. The architecture scales efficiently to datasets spanning hundreds of thousands of blocks, substantially reducing analyst workload in financial feasibility studies. Shapley Additive Explanation (SHAP) analysis reveals the relative contribution of each input variable to profitability outcomes, enabling targeted operational interventions. The underlying pipeline is commodity-agnostic and can be adapted for gold, lithium, or other metallic deposits with minimal reconfiguration.

title: The Bulk-Synchronous Parallel Model
summary:
Leslie Valiant [1990a] proposed the bulk-synchronous parallel (BSP) model in a seminal paper (reprinted here) as an efficient bridge between parallel software and parallel hardware. At a time when parallel computers were just emerging and still only available on a limited scale, often as expensive supercomputers, their archi tectures were diverging and programming them could be totally different from machine to machine. The sequential situation was the opposite: the von Neumann model of a processor with its connected memory provided a unifying abstract tar get machine for which algorithms could be designed and their time complexity analyzed. The BSP model changed the situation for the parallel case by providing such a unifying model.
Separation of concerns is a sound engineering principle, which in the context of computers translates to the main concerns of building hardware and writing software. A designer of parallel hardware should only be concerned about build ing a computer architecture with optimal characteristics such as high processor speed, high communication bandwidth, and low latency, whereas a designer of parallel software should take these as given and write the best possible program, only worrying about the time complexity of the operations carried out during com putation, communication, and synchronization. The success of the von Neumann model is due to the clear separation it provides between such concerns for sequen tial computations, and the BSP model is intended to do the same for the parallel case.

title: Evolution of Industry 5.0 using AI based AMRs in Industrial Private 5G Network
summary: Artificial Intelligence (AI)-enabled Autonomous Mobile Robots (AMRs) are transforming industrial operations across manufacturing and logistics - accounting for 65% of new deployments in 2025 and displacing traditional Automated Guided Vehicles (AGVs) through superior navigation, flexibility, and autonomous decision-making. This paper examines the evolution and integration of AMRs with Private 5G networks in industrial applications. Traditional connectivity options, namely: wired networks, Wi-Fi, and public cellular, cannot meet the mobility, reliability, and latency requirements of industrial AMR deployments. Private 5G networks address these limitations through deterministic performance, dedicated spectrum, and enterprise-grade security. Our comparative analysis establishes AMRs’ performance advantages over AGVs and Private 5G’s operational superiority versus alternative connectivity approaches. In this work, we examine the computing architectures supporting AMR systems (local, edge, centralized, and hybrid), each with distinct implications for safety-critical industrial deployments. The integration of AI/ML with distributed intelligence and human-robot collaboration requires consistent, low-latency communication, particularly for safety-critical and shared workflows. This AMR-Private 5G integration positions industrial operations at the threshold of Industry 5.0, enabling autonomous, adaptive systems that enhance operational flexibility, safety, and productivity.
